_about: Single source of truth for every rendering, and the auditable term ledger (check 5). ONE rendering per referent for the whole book. Before you romanize any name, check here. status per entry: 'attested' (form used in English scholarship, give the citation in note), 'provisional' (your romanization, not found in outside sources), 'decided' (a project style call). If you find a better attested form mid-book, change it here AND grep every built chapter for the old form, then rebuild. Sections are rendered as glossary headings; keys starting with '_' are ignored. Add/rename sections freely (people, organizations, places, terms, ...).

风萧萧.note: The novel's title. It quotes the opening of the parting song sung for the assassin Jing Ke at the Yi River, 风萧萧兮易水寒 (‘the wind whistles, cold runs the Yi’); the note of doomed, high-minded sacrifice governs the book.

徐訏.note: Chinese writer (1908–1980), the novel's author; original name Xu Chuanzong (徐傳琮), pen name Xu Xu. Pinyin form standard in English-language scholarship (older romanization Hsu Yu).

史蒂芬.note: C. L. Stephen, the American naval surgeon; 史蒂芬 transliterates the English name Stephen, restored here.

白苹.note: A dancer at the Paramount, secretly a Chinese agent. Pinyin; 苹 read ping.

梅瀛子.note: A dazzling Eurasian socialite; her father was Chinese (long resident in Japan), her mother American. Pinyin.

海伦.note: Helen Manfield, a shy, music-loving young American. 海伦 = Helen.

曼斐儿.note: Helen's surname; 曼斐儿 transliterates a Western surname whose exact original spelling the source does not give. ‘Manfield’ is a plausible reconstruction.

费利普.note: The surgeon whose clinic Stephen uses; the source spells the name two ways (费利普 and 菲利浦), both transliterating Philip/Phillips.

高.note: Mr. Gao, the Chinese manager of the Weibai Hotel; his American wife and their daughter, Miss Gao, appear at Stephen's party.

工部局乐队.note: The orchestra of the Shanghai Municipal Council (工部局), long led by Mario Paci; in its day the most celebrated orchestra in the Far East.

北京大学.note: Conventional English name of the university; Xu Xu read philosophy there.

百乐门.note: The Paramount Ballroom (百乐门) on Bubbling Well Road, Shanghai's most famous dance hall.

辣斐德路.note: A street in the French Concession (today Fuxing Middle Road).

静安寺路.note: Major road in the International Settlement, named for the Jing'an (Bubbling Well) Temple; today Nanjing West Road.

麦特赫司脱路.note: A road off Bubbling Well Road (today Taixing Road); the source also spells it 麦特赫斯脱路.

愚园路.note: A road running west from the Jing'an area.

霞飞路.note: The French Concession's main thoroughfare, lined with cafés and shops (today Huaihai Middle Road).

海格路.note: A road on the western edge of the Settlement (today Huashan Road).

善锺路.note: A French Concession street (today Changshu Road); source form 善锺路.

贝当路.note: A French Concession road (today Hengshan Road).

四马路.note: Popular Shanghai nickname (one of the numbered ‘horse roads’) for the settlement's Foochow Road, today Fuzhou Road, known for small restaurants, bookshops and nightlife.

徐家汇.note: District in the southwest of Shanghai (older form Zikawei/Ziccawei), site of the Jesuit St Ignatius Cathedral.

仁济医院.note: A long-established Shanghai hospital (Shanghai's first Western hospital, founded 1844), known to foreigners as the Chinese Hospital or Shantung Road Hospital.

维纳斯.note: A dance hall; 维纳斯 = Venus.

丽都.note: A Shanghai dance hall / entertainment venue.

凯莎舞厅.note: A dance hall; romanization of 凯莎.

立体咖啡馆.note: A café near the corner of Bubbling Well and Medhurst Roads; 立体 means ‘solid’ or ‘three-dimensional’.

大华电影院.note: A Shanghai picture house; 大华 was the Chinese name of the Majestic.

芭口公寓.note: The apartment building where Mrs. Manfield lives; 芭口 transliterates a Western name not identified in the source (pinyin romanization used here).

魏白饭店.note: A hotel managed by Mr. Gao; 魏白 transliterates a Western name not identified in the source.

孤岛.note: The name for the foreign-concession enclave of Shanghai between the Japanese occupation of the surrounding city in 1937 and the seizure of the concessions after Pearl Harbor in December 1941, during which the concessions kept a precarious neutral status.

鬼恋.note: Xu Xu's 1937 novella, the work that made his name.

江湖行.note: Xu Xu's later long novel, published 1956–1961; rendered River of Fury in the scholarship of Frederik Green. The Chinese 江湖行 means ‘a journey through the rivers and lakes’ (the itinerant world).
